#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/). AndeSim supports 64-bit
# RISC-V only, so there is one output:
#   build/runtime/   libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
#                    include/andesim/ROI.h
# Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`.
#
# Self-contained: fills HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN from config.env (exported env wins),
# like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }

# Capture the exported value (it wins), then source config.env to fill the gap.
ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi
[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"

if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$SRC" TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a"
===== fixtures Makefile =====
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# AndeSim supports 64-bit RISC-V only, so these are the only tools. The check is
# deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so a target that needs a
# DIFFERENT toolchain (the LINUX_TOOLCHAIN glibc fixtures) still builds without
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN set.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window
# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Contract: tests/e2e.sh is a self-contained QEMU+vsim handoff harness and must
# NOT shell out to the andesim driver. Differential oracle verification lives in
# the product path `andesim run --verify` (see test_andes_sim_verify.sh), so
# e2e.sh carries no `andesim state-diff` call and no VERIFY=1 leg. Comments may
# still mention the driver for context -- only an executable dependency fails.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The entry point's container contract (F4 + issue #20).
#
# Every `andesim` run happens inside the prebuilt AndeSim image: both hybrid
# legs must share one Linux kernel, and the image is what carries QEMU, the
# cycle-accurate engine and the driver. macOS has always worked this way; from
# issue #20 Linux does too, so a user who built the image never composes a
# container invocation.
#
# Four rules make a containerised run behave like a local one:
#   1. The shared mmap stays container-local: the container's /dev/shm
#      (--shm-size) is tier 1, sized from the run's own --mem-size but never
#      past what the host has free, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never
#      forwarded -- a host path would be a virtiofs mount on macOS, where
#      MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
#   4. A missing image is reported as a missing image, not as container noise.
#
# Verified with a stub container engine, so no image and no run are needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

IMAGE="andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")"
MIB=$((1024 * 1024))
GIB=$((1024 * 1024 * 1024))
# The driver demands this much free space beyond the mmap it is about to
# allocate (kMmapSafetyMargin, driver/shm.hpp), so /dev/shm must carry it too.
MARGIN=$((256 * MIB))

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t andes-container.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Stub engine: answers the image-existence probe from STUB_IMAGES, records the
# argv of a `run`, and executes nothing.
cat > "$TMP/stub-engine" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "image" ]; then
  grep -qxF -- "$3" "${STUB_IMAGES:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null
  exit $?
fi
printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_OUT"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/stub-engine"

printf '%s\n' "$IMAGE" > "$TMP/images"          # the image is built
: > "$TMP/no-images"                            # ...and here it is not

# argv_of OUT ARG...  -- run the entry point from $TMP against the stub engine
# and echo the container argv it produced. ENV_EXTRA adds per-case env; ENTRY
# names the entry point to invoke (a case drives it through a symlink).
ENV_EXTRA=()
ENTRY="$ROOT/andesim"
argv_of() {
  local out="$TMP/$1"; shift
  (cd "$TMP" && env STUB_OUT="$out" STUB_IMAGES="$TMP/images" \
     ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
     HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/host/scratch \
     "${ENV_EXTRA[@]}" \
     "$ENTRY" "$@" </dev/null) || fail "entry point exited non-zero: $*"
  [ -f "$out" ] || fail "stub engine was never invoked for: $*"
  cat "$out"
}

# --- 1. a run goes into the image, with nothing asked of the user -----------
ARGV=$(argv_of argv run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf)

has() { printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qxF -- "$1"; }

has "run"        || fail "engine argv missing 'run':"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--shm-size" || fail "missing --shm-size (container-local mmap tier 1):"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "$TMP:$TMP"  || fail "cwd not bind-mounted at the same path:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "-w"         || fail "missing workdir:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "my.elf"     || fail "user args not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--mem-size" || fail "user flags not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "$IMAGE"     || fail "default image name ($IMAGE) absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -q "HSIM_MMAP_DIR" \
  && fail "HSIM_MMAP_DIR must not cross into the container:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qxF -- "-it" \
  && fail "no TTY here, so -it must be absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"

# The image declares its own ENTRYPOINT, so the user's first argument must
# follow the image name directly.
AFTER=$(printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -nxF -- "$IMAGE" | cut -d: -f1)
[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | sed -n "$((AFTER + 1))p")" = "run" ] \
  || fail "the user's first argument does not follow the image:"$'\n'"$ARGV"

ok "a run executes inside $IMAGE, cwd mounted at the same path, args verbatim"

# --- 2. /dev/shm is sized from the run's own --mem-size ---------------------
# A hybrid run maps --mem-size bytes of guest RAM out of /dev/shm, and the
# driver refuses a tier without MARGIN to spare. A container's default 64 MB
# fails the standard tests; a fixed constant cannot serve both a 128M run and
# an 8G one -- so the size must follow the run.
to_bytes() {
  awk '{ u = tolower(substr($0, length($0))); v = $0 + 0
         if (u == "k") v *= 1024
         else if (u == "m") v *= 1048576
         else if (u == "g") v *= 1073741824
         else if (u == "t") v *= 1099511627776
         printf "%d\n", v }' <<<"$1"
}
shm_bytes() {  # the value following --shm-size, in bytes
  to_bytes "$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -A1 -xF -- '--shm-size' | tail -1)"
}

# The host's free shared memory: the ceiling this machine imposes (issue #28).
HOST_FREE=$(df -Pk /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 2 { printf "%d", $4 * 1024 }')
[ -n "$HOST_FREE" ] || HOST_FREE=$((3 * GIB))

# shm_fits TAG WANT ARGV -- WANT bytes of guest RAM must fit, with the
# driver's margin, and without over-reserving by more than one further GiB
# (an over-generous constant would not be "sized from the run"). A run the
# host cannot back is capped instead -- see the ceiling case below.
shm_fits() {
  local tag="$1" want="$2" got; got=$(shm_bytes "$3")
  if [ "$((want + MARGIN))" -gt "$HOST_FREE" ]; then
    [ "$got" -le "$HOST_FREE" ] \
      || fail "$tag: --shm-size $got exceeds the host's free shared memory:"$'\n'"$3"
    return
  fi
  [ "$got" -ge "$((want + MARGIN))" ] \
    || fail "$tag: --shm-size $got is too small for ${want}B + margin:"$'\n'"$3"
  [ "$got" -le "$((want + MARGIN + GIB))" ] \
    || fail "$tag: --shm-size $got is not sized from the run (${want}B asked):"$'\n'"$3"
}

shm_fits "--mem-size 8G" $((8 * GIB)) \
  "$(argv_of argv-8g run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 8G my.elf)"
shm_fits "--mem-size 128M" $((128 * MIB)) \
  "$(argv_of argv-128m run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 128M my.elf)"
shm_fits "--mem-size=1G (joined spelling)" "$GIB" \
  "$(argv_of argv-eq run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size=1G my.elf)"
# No --mem-size: --runtime linux defaults to 1G (driver/cmd_run.cpp), the
# largest default, so the run must still fit without the user saying so.
shm_fits "no --mem-size" "$GIB" \
  "$(argv_of argv-default run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux my.elf)"

ok "/dev/shm is sized from the run's --mem-size, with the driver's margin"

# --- the ceiling: never promise more shared memory than the host has --------
# Issue #28. /dev/shm is RAM. The driver's tier list protects the machine only
# because a run that does not fit can FALL PAST tier 1 to disk. Sizing tier 1
# to always fit removed that: the fallback could not happen any more, and a
# run larger than the machine took the machine down instead of going slow.
BIG=$(argv_of argv-huge run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 900G my.elf)
[ "$(shm_bytes "$BIG")" -le "$HOST_FREE" ] \
  || fail "a 900G run was promised more shared memory than the host has free"$'\n'"$BIG"

# The ceiling is a knob, so a user can hold a run below what the host would
# otherwise hand out -- and so both halves of the rule are testable.
ENV_EXTRA=(ANDESIM_SHM_MAX=512m)
[ "$(shm_bytes "$(argv_of argv-cap run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 8G my.elf)")" \
    = "$((512 * MIB))" ] \
  || fail "ANDESIM_SHM_MAX did not cap an 8G run"

# Never below the 64 MiB a container gets by default: past that point the
# driver falls to its next tier anyway, and asking for less buys nothing.
ENV_EXTRA=(ANDESIM_SHM_MAX=1m)
[ "$(shm_bytes "$(argv_of argv-floor run --mode fast my.elf)")" = "$((64 * MIB))" ] \
  || fail "the ceiling went below the container's own 64 MiB default"
ENV_EXTRA=()

ok "/dev/shm stops at the host's free shared memory, so the tier fallback still works"

# --- 3. the overrides stay --------------------------------------------------
ENV_EXTRA=(ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE=7g)
[ "$(shm_bytes "$(argv_of argv-shm run --mode fast my.elf)")" = "$((7 * GIB))" ] \
  || fail "ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE not honored"

printf '%s\n' "$IMAGE" registry.example/andes:v2 > "$TMP/images"
ENV_EXTRA=(ANDESIM_IMAGE=registry.example/andes:v2)
argv_of argv-img run --mode fast my.elf | grep -qxF -- registry.example/andes:v2 \
  || fail "ANDESIM_IMAGE not honored"

ENV_EXTRA=()
printf '%s\n' "$IMAGE" > "$TMP/images"

ok "ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE and ANDESIM_IMAGE still override"

# --- 4. no image: a message the user can act on, not container noise --------
OUT=$( (cd "$TMP" && env STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv-none" STUB_IMAGES="$TMP/no-images" \
          ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
          "$ROOT/andesim" run --mode fast my.elf </dev/null) 2>&1 )
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -ne 0 ] || fail "a missing image must fail the run, got rc=0:"$'\n'"$OUT"
[ -f "$TMP/argv-none" ] \
  && fail "a container was started although no image exists:"$'\n'"$(cat "$TMP/argv-none")"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qF -- "$IMAGE" \
  || fail "the missing-image message does not name the image:"$'\n'"$OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qF -- 'scripts/build_image.sh' \
  || fail "the missing-image message does not say how to build it:"$'\n'"$OUT"

ok "a missing image is reported as a missing image, with the command to build it"

# --- 5. the native development path is still reachable ----------------------
# Issue #20 makes the container the default, not the only way: a developer
# still runs the driver built in this working tree.
require_driver
NATIVE=$( (cd "$TMP" && env ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1 \
             STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv-native" STUB_IMAGES="$TMP/images" \
             ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
             "$ROOT/andesim" --version </dev/null) 2>&1 ) \
  || fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$NATIVE"
[ -f "$TMP/argv-native" ] \
  && fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER still went through the container"
[ "$NATIVE" = "$("$BIN" --version 2>&1)" ] \
  || fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER did not run the locally built driver:"$'\n'"$NATIVE"

ok "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1 keeps the native development path"

# --- 6. the entry point survives a symlink on PATH --------------------------
# Putting a command on PATH means symlinking it into a bin directory. The
# wrapper reaches sideways for scripts/run_in_container.sh, so it has to
# resolve its own path to the real file: beside the LINK there is no scripts/
# directory, and the user got rc=127 and a raw "No such file or directory".
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
ln -sf "$ROOT/andesim" "$TMP/bin/andesim"
ENTRY="$TMP/bin/andesim"
argv_of argv-link run --mode fast my.elf | grep -qxF -- "$IMAGE" \
  || fail "a symlinked entry point does not reach the image"
ENTRY="$ROOT/andesim"

ok "the entry point works through a symlink on PATH"

ok "container run contract (stubbed container engine)"

RC=$?
[ "$RC" -ne 0 ] || fail "a missing image must fail the run, got rc=0:"$'\n'"$OUT"
[ -f "$TMP/argv-none" ] \
  && fail "a container was started although no image exists:"$'\n'"$(cat "$TMP/argv-none")"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qF -- "$IMAGE" \
  || fail "the missing-image message does not name the image:"$'\n'"$OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qF -- 'scripts/build_image.sh' \
  || fail "the missing-image message does not say how to build it:"$'\n'"$OUT"

ok "a missing image is reported as a missing image, with the command to build it"

# --- 5. the native development path is still reachable ----------------------
# Issue #20 makes the container the default, not the only way: a developer
# still runs the driver built in this working tree.
require_driver
NATIVE=$( (cd "$TMP" && env ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1 \
             STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv-native" STUB_IMAGES="$TMP/images" \
             ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
             "$ROOT/andesim" --version </dev/null) 2>&1 ) \
  || fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$NATIVE"
[ -f "$TMP/argv-native" ] \
  && fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER still went through the container"
[ "$NATIVE" = "$("$BIN" --version 2>&1)" ] \
  || fail "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER did not run the locally built driver:"$'\n'"$NATIVE"

ok "ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1 keeps the native development path"

# --- 6. the entry point survives a symlink on PATH --------------------------
# Putting a command on PATH means symlinking it into a bin directory. The
# wrapper reaches sideways for scripts/run_in_container.sh, so it has to
# resolve its own path to the real file: beside the LINK there is no scripts/
# directory, and the user got rc=127 and a raw "No such file or directory".
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
ln -sf "$ROOT/andesim" "$TMP/bin/andesim"
ENTRY="$TMP/bin/andesim"
argv_of argv-link run --mode fast my.elf | grep -qxF -- "$IMAGE" \
  || fail "a symlinked entry point does not reach the image"
ENTRY="$ROOT/andesim"

ok "the entry point works through a symlink on PATH"

ok "container run contract (stubbed container engine)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   lint      tests/test_*.sh + roi.test.sh + the fixture ROI-content lint
#             (fast harness self-checks; no engine spawns. The one heavy
#             harness test, tests/test_kernel_cycles.sh, stays manual: it
#             runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips the e2e phase already covers.)
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

# --version's build-time half: the release tag plus the git identity of this
# checkout and of the shared ABI submodule, stamped into the binary. Re-run on
# EVERY build, not just at configure time -- a stale stamp would let the binary
# claim a commit it was not built from, the very source/binary mix-up the report
# exists to expose. The header is rewritten only when the values change, so an
# unchanged checkout costs nothing.
set(ANDESIM_GENERATED_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated)
add_custom_target(andesim-build-stamp ALL
  BYPRODUCTS ${ANDESIM_GENERATED_DIR}/build_stamp.h
  COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND}
          -DREPO_ROOT=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/..
          -DABI_ROOT=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include
          -DVERSION_FILE=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../VERSION
          -DOUT=${ANDESIM_GENERATED_DIR}/build_stamp.h
          -P ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/build_stamp.cmake
  COMMENT "andesim: stamping build identity"
  VERBATIM)

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  cmd_profile.cpp
  cmd_version.cpp
  version.cpp
  profile.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  log.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
  memmap.cpp
  manifest.cpp
  tempdir.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up;
# build_stamp.h is generated next to the objects by andesim-build-stamp.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include
                                           ${ANDESIM_GENERATED_DIR})
add_dependencies(andesim andesim-build-stamp)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp tempdir.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp engine_registry.cpp tempdir.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp log.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp log.cpp)
# hybrid guest memory-map composer (pure; descriptor + qemu.cfg text in, rows out).
add_executable(andesim-memmap-test memmap_test.cpp memmap.cpp shm.cpp log.cpp)
# profile core: plugin-log/disasm parsing, RVV filter, loop nesting, renderers,
# QEMU argv builder (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-profile-test profile_test.cpp profile.cpp)
# U2 (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): .manifest blob + objcopy argv builder, plus
# make_temp_dir (pure/fast; the real copy+objcopy spawn is a shell-level test).
add_executable(andesim-manifest-test manifest_test.cpp manifest.cpp tempdir.cpp process.cpp log.cpp)
# U10c: vlinux's guest-RAM address math (runtime/linux/vlinux_mem.h) -- header
# only, so no runtime/linux source is linked (that code is RISC-V bare-metal).
add_executable(andesim-vlinux-mem-test vlinux_mem_test.cpp)
# --version's report core: the qemu/engine --version output parsers and the
# renderer (pure; the collection side lives in cmd_version.cpp).
add_executable(andesim-version-test version_test.cpp version.cpp)

foreach(_t andesim-cli-test andesim-json-test andesim-infra-test andesim-plan-test andesim-plan-itest andesim-run-test andesim-vsimfilter-test andesim-elf-syms-test andesim-hybrid-test andesim-state-diff-test andesim-engine-registry-test andesim-memmap-test andesim-profile-test andesim-manifest-test andesim-vlinux-mem-test andesim-version-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-state-diff-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# memmap reads HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (the reserved top page) from the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-memmap-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# hybrid-test reaches plan.hpp via hybrid.hpp; plan.hpp carries the drained
# record (hybrid_state_v1) since verify_oracle F4.
target_include_directories(andesim-hybrid-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# elf-syms-test: find_roi_markers (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9) reads the
# shared marker predicate, hybrid/insn_match.h.
target_include_directories(andesim-elf-syms-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# U10c: vlinux_mem.h reserves the top HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES from the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-vlinux-mem-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

# Shared status printers + config/path resolution for test scripts.
# Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#   cfg_val KEY            -> KEY's value from the repo-root config.env
#   vsim_bin_dir           -> external vsim build dir (env, then config.env)
#   qemu_bin               -> path to qemu-system-riscv64, same
#                             env-then-config.env resolution
#   shipped_cycle_engines  -> cycle-accurate engine names v0.1.0 ships
#   deferred_cycle_engines -> the ones it does not (later releases)
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# ENGINE RELEASE SURFACE -- one source of truth for the whole harness.
# v0.1.0 ships exactly two cycle-accurate engines, and the vsim side builds
# only these two (its config.yaml). Every other CPU config is deferred to a
# later release; with ax66_makatau went S/U-privilege handoff support --
# ax45mpv_premium is M-mode-only (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1) while
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 carries all three levels, so re-enabling S/U there is future
# work, not a v0.1.0 promise. test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh enforces that no
# test in the harness pins a deferred engine.
shipped_cycle_engines() { echo "ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_fpga_l3"; }
deferred_cycle_engines() {
  echo "ax45mpv_premium_full ax45mpv_premium_max ax46mpv_advanced" \
       "ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw ax66_makatau d23"
}

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

# The external QEMU build dir, resolved the same way: QEMU_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env ("" when neither is set).
qemu_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$QEMU_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR
}

# qemu_bin -> full path of qemu-system-riscv64 in that dir (AndeSim supports
# 64-bit RISC-V only).
qemu_bin() { printf '%s/qemu-system-riscv64\n' "$(qemu_bin_dir)"; }

# Quiet driver self-build (the byte-identical preamble line of every driver
# contract test). Fatal on build failure.
build_driver() {
  bash "$_LIB_ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
}

# build_driver + point BIN at the driver binary. The caller keeps its own
# [ -x "$BIN" ] assertion (the failure messages vary per script).
require_driver() {
  BIN="$_LIB_ROOT/build/andesim"
  build_driver
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #22 -- `--help` is layered, and it is COMPLETE.
#
#   * `andesim --help` is an OVERVIEW: what the tool is and which commands it
#     has. It does not reprint every option of every command.
#   * `andesim <cmd> --help` carries that command's COMPLETE option list, plus
#     runnable examples.
#   * Every option a command ACCEPTS appears in that command's help. An option
#     the tool takes but never names cannot be found by a user.
#
# The accepted set is not a list this file keeps in step by hand. It is
# harvested from the option table's own source, and then each candidate is
# offered to each command and the BINARY says whether it took it: the parser
# finishes before `--help` is honoured, so the probe starts no engine and
# needs no ELF.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

require_driver
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

COMMANDS="run profile list doctor"

# --- the candidate options --------------------------------------------------
# Every `"--flag"` literal in the parser's own sources. Harvested rather than
# listed, so an option added to the parser and forgotten in the help is caught
# by this test instead of by a user. `-h` is added by hand: it is the one
# single-dash spelling, and no `--` regex can find it.
SRCS=()
for f in "$ROOT/driver/options.cpp" "$ROOT/driver/cli.cpp"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && SRCS+=("$f")
done
[ "${#SRCS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no parser source to harvest options from"

FLAGS=$( { grep -ohE '"--[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*"' "${SRCS[@]}" | tr -d '"'
           echo "-h"; } | sort -u )
[ -n "$FLAGS" ] || fail "harvested no options from ${SRCS[*]}"
echo "[info] candidate options: $(echo $FLAGS | tr '\n' ' ')"

# --- the two questions asked of each (command, option) pair -----------------

# accepts CMD FLAG -- true when the PARSER takes FLAG for CMD. A dummy value
# follows so a value-taking option is satisfied; a switch simply gains a
# positional that `--help` then makes irrelevant.
accepts() {
  local cmd="$1" flag="$2" out
  out=$("$BIN" "$cmd" "$flag" 1 --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
  ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- "unknown option: $flag\$|$flag is not a"
}

# documented CMD FLAG -- true when CMD's help names FLAG as a whole word, so
# `--gdb` is not satisfied by `--gdb-port` and `--llm` is not by `--no-llm`.
documented() {
  local cmd="$1" flag="$2"
  "$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null \
    | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)"
}

# --- 1. every accepted option is discoverable -------------------------------
missing=""
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  for flag in $FLAGS; do
    accepts "$cmd" "$flag" || continue
    documented "$cmd" "$flag" || missing="$missing"$'\n'"  $cmd accepts $flag, '$cmd --help' does not name it"
  done
done
[ -z "$missing" ] || fail "options accepted but undocumented:$missing"
ok "every option a command accepts appears in that command's help"

# --- 2. each command's help carries runnable examples -----------------------
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  H=$("$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
  printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*andesim ' \
    || fail "'$cmd --help' has no runnable example (a line starting 'andesim ...'):"$'\n'"$H"
done
ok "every command's help carries at least one runnable example"

# --- 3. the top level is an overview, not every option ----------------------
TOP=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE "^$cmd " \
    || fail "the overview does not list the command '$cmd':"$'\n'"$TOP"
done
# A command's own knobs belong in that command's help. Their presence here is
# what "lists every option of every subcommand" looks like.
for flag in --pc-start --kanata --gdb-port --min-iters --addr2line --raw; do
  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)" \
    && fail "the overview reprints a command's own option '$flag':"$'\n'"$TOP"
done
printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -q -- '--help' \
  || fail "the overview does not point at the per-command help:"$'\n'"$TOP"
ok "the top level is an overview: the commands, not every command's options"

ok "layered, complete --help (issue #22)"

FLAGS=$( { grep -ohE '"--[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*"' "${SRCS[@]}" | tr -d '"'
           echo "-h"; } | sort -u )
[ -n "$FLAGS" ] || fail "harvested no options from ${SRCS[*]}"
echo "[info] candidate options: $(echo $FLAGS | tr '\n' ' ')"

# --- the two questions asked of each (command, option) pair -----------------

# accepts CMD FLAG -- true when the PARSER takes FLAG for CMD. A dummy value
# follows so a value-taking option is satisfied; a switch simply gains a
# positional that `--help` then makes irrelevant.
accepts() {
  local cmd="$1" flag="$2" out
  out=$("$BIN" "$cmd" "$flag" 1 --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
  ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- "unknown option: $flag\$|$flag is not a"
}

# documented CMD FLAG -- true when CMD's help names FLAG as a whole word, so
# `--gdb` is not satisfied by `--gdb-port` and `--llm` is not by `--no-llm`.
documented() {
  local cmd="$1" flag="$2"
  "$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null \
    | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)"
}

# --- 1. every accepted option is discoverable -------------------------------
missing=""
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  for flag in $FLAGS; do
    accepts "$cmd" "$flag" || continue
    documented "$cmd" "$flag" || missing="$missing"$'\n'"  $cmd accepts $flag, '$cmd --help' does not name it"
  done
done
[ -z "$missing" ] || fail "options accepted but undocumented:$missing"
ok "every option a command accepts appears in that command's help"

# --- 2. each command's help carries runnable examples -----------------------
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  H=$("$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
  printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*andesim ' \
    || fail "'$cmd --help' has no runnable example (a line starting 'andesim ...'):"$'\n'"$H"
done
ok "every command's help carries at least one runnable example"

# --- 3. the top level is an overview, not every option ----------------------
TOP=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE "^$cmd " \
    || fail "the overview does not list the command '$cmd':"$'\n'"$TOP"
done
# A command's own knobs belong in that command's help. Their presence here is
# what "lists every option of every subcommand" looks like.
for flag in --pc-start --kanata --gdb-port --min-iters --addr2line --raw; do
  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)" \
    && fail "the overview reprints a command's own option '$flag':"$'\n'"$TOP"
done
printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -q -- '--help' \
  || fail "the overview does not point at the per-command help:"$'\n'"$TOP"
ok "the top level is an overview: the commands, not every command's options"

ok "layered, complete --help (issue #22)"

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, profile, list, doctor) and never the third-party
4	# simulator name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff
5	# have moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
6	# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
7	# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
8	# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
9	# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
10	# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
11	# must come back out as vsim:.
12	set -uo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
17	
18	require_driver
19	
20	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
21	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
22	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
23	
24	# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
25	# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
26	# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
27	# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
28	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
29	has '^run '     "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
30	has '^profile ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'profile':"$'\n'"$H"
31	has '^list '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
32	has '^doctor '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
33	for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
34	  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
35	done
36	for t in models engines; do
37	  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
38	done
39	has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
40	for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
41	  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
42	done
43	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
44	has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
45	has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
46	ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"
47	
48	# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
49	# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
50	# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run andesim inside the AndeSim image (see Containerfile, built by
3	# scripts/build_image.sh). This is where a run lives: both hybrid legs must
4	# share one Linux kernel, and the image carries QEMU, the cycle-accurate
5	# engine and the driver.
6	#
7	# Four rules make a containerised run behave like a local one:
8	#   1. The shared mmap stays container-local: the container's /dev/shm
9	#      (--shm-size) is tier 1, sized from the run's own --mem-size but never
10	#      past what the host has free, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never
11	#      forwarded -- a host path would be a virtiofs mount on macOS, where
12	#      MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
13	#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
14	#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
15	#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
16	#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
17	#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
18	#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
19	#   4. A missing image is reported as a missing image. Left to the container
20	#      runtime it surfaces as a pull failure against a registry that was
21	#      never meant to hold it -- v0.1.0 publishes no image; each user builds
22	#      their own.
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
26	
27	# The canonical in-image toolchain mount point, shared with the image build.
28	IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
29	
30	# Sizing constants, mirrored from the driver so the container's /dev/shm
31	# matches what the driver will ask of it:
32	#   V_SCRATCH  the V-register transport page mapped ABOVE the program's RAM
33	#              (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, include/hybrid/state_abi.h)
34	#   MMAP_MARGIN free space the tier resolver demands beyond the mmap itself
35	#              (kMmapSafetyMargin, driver/shm.hpp)
36	#   DEFAULT_MEM the largest --mem-size default the driver applies when the
37	#              user names none (--runtime linux's 1G, driver/cmd_run.cpp)
38	V_SCRATCH=$((32 * 128))
39	MMAP_MARGIN=$((256 * 1024 * 1024))
40	DEFAULT_MEM=$((1024 * 1024 * 1024))
41	MIB=$((1024 * 1024))
42	
43	# The ceiling on tier 1, and the floor below which capping buys nothing:
44	#   VM_SHM_CEILING  what a macOS run may take. There the container lives in
45	#                   the podman-machine VM and the host has no /dev/shm to
46	#                   measure, so the VM-local value stands.
47	#   SHM_FLOOR       the 64 MiB a container gets by default. Past that the
48	#                   driver falls to its next tier anyway.
49	VM_SHM_CEILING=$((3 * 1024 * MIB))
50	SHM_FLOOR=$((64 * MIB))
51	
52	# to_bytes SPEC DEFAULT  -- "8G" / "512m" / "1024" in bytes. DEFAULT stands in
53	# for an empty or malformed spec: a bad --mem-size is for the driver to report,
54	# with the whole spec in hand, and must not silently shrink /dev/shm here.
55	to_bytes() {
56	  awk -v s="$1" -v def="$2" 'BEGIN {
57	    v = s + 0
58	    u = tolower(substr(s, length(s)))
59	    if (u == "k") v *= 1024
60	    else if (u == "m") v *= 1048576
61	    else if (u == "g") v *= 1073741824
62	    else if (u == "t") v *= 1099511627776
63	    printf "%d\n", (v > 0 ? v : def)
64	  }'
65	}
66	
67	# guest_mem_spec ARG...  -- the last --mem-size on the line, which is the one
68	# the driver keeps.
69	guest_mem_spec() {
70	  local spec="" prev="" a
71	  for a in "$@"; do
72	    case "$prev" in --mem-size) spec="$a" ;; esac
73	    case "$a" in --mem-size=*) spec="${a#*=}" ;; esac
74	    prev="$a"
75	  done
76	  printf '%s\n' "$spec"
77	}
78	
79	# shm_ceiling  -- the most shared memory this container may be offered.
80	#
81	# /dev/shm is RAM. The driver's tier list -- /dev/shm, then a disk directory --
82	# protects the machine only because a run too big for memory can FALL PAST
83	# tier 1 and finish slowly on disk. Sizing tier 1 to always fit removed that
84	# protection: the fallback could no longer happen, and a run larger than the
85	# machine took the machine down instead of going slow. So the size follows the
86	# run, but stops at what the host itself could have given a native run.
87	shm_ceiling() {
88	  local cap
89	  cap=$(df -Pk /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 2 { printf "%d", $4 * 1024 }')
90	  [ -n "$cap" ] || cap="$VM_SHM_CEILING"   # no host /dev/shm: the run is in a VM
91	  [ -z "${ANDESIM_SHM_MAX:-}" ] || cap=$(to_bytes "$ANDESIM_SHM_MAX" "$cap")
92	  [ "$cap" -ge "$SHM_FLOOR" ] || cap="$SHM_FLOOR"
93	  printf '%s\n' "$cap"
94	}
95	
96	# shm_size_for ARG...  -- the --shm-size this command line needs, in whole
97	# MiB. A hybrid run maps its guest RAM out of /dev/shm; a container's default
98	# 64 MB is below even the standard tests, and no fixed value serves both a
99	# 128M run and an 8G one, so the size follows the run -- up to the ceiling.
100	shm_size_for() {
101	  local mem want want_mib cap_mib
102	  mem=$(to_bytes "$(guest_mem_spec "$@")" "$DEFAULT_MEM")
103	  want=$((mem + V_SCRATCH + MMAP_MARGIN))
104	  want_mib=$(((want + MIB - 1) / MIB))          # round up: the run must fit
105	  cap_mib=$(($(shm_ceiling) / MIB))             # round down: the host must not overcommit
106	  [ "$want_mib" -le "$cap_mib" ] || want_mib="$cap_mib"
107	  printf '%dm\n' "$want_mib"
108	}
109	
110	ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
111	if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
112	  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
113	  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
114	  else
115	    echo "andesim: a run executes inside the AndeSim image and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
116	    echo "           on macOS also: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
117	    exit 2
118	  fi
119	fi
120	
121	# VERSION is the single source of truth for the tag scripts/build_image.sh
122	# applies, so a version bump cannot desync the build from the run.
123	IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)}"
124	
125	if ! "$ENGINE" image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
126	  echo "andesim: no image named $IMAGE on this machine." >&2
127	  echo "           AndeSim runs inside an image you build once:" >&2
128	  echo "             scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <riscv-toolchain-root>" >&2
129	  exit 2
130	fi
131	
132	SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-$(shm_size_for "$@")}"
133	
134	# The image declares its own ENTRYPOINT, so the user's arguments go straight
135	# to it. Passing the entry path as an argument as well made the driver see its
136	# own path as an operand ("unexpected argument 'run'"). ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY
137	# stays available as an override, applied the only way that works.
138	ENTRY_ARGS=()
139	if [ -n "${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-}" ]; then
140	  ENTRY_ARGS=(--entrypoint "$ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY")
141	fi
142	
143	# The toolchain the caller has: the exported value, else config.env's.
144	TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
145	if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
146	  TOOLCHAIN=$(sed -n 's/^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=//p' "$ROOT/config.env" | tr -d '"' | head -1)
147	fi
148	TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=()
149	if [ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -d "$TOOLCHAIN" ]; then
150	  TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=(-v "$TOOLCHAIN:$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN:ro")
151	fi
152	
153	TTY_ARGS=()
154	if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi
155	
156	exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
157	  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
158	  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
159	  "${TOOLCHAIN_ARGS[@]}" \
160	  -w "$PWD" \
161	  "${ENTRY_ARGS[@]}" \
162	  "$IMAGE" "$@"

2	#
3	# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
4	# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
5	# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
6	#
7	# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
8	# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
9	# build/andesim.
10	cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
11	project(andes_sim CXX)
12	
13	set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14	set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

17	if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)

20

usage: andesim <command> [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]

Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).
64-bit RISC-V only: 32-bit workloads and engines are not supported.

run     run one simulation (the default: 'run' may be omitted)
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed
  cycle     one cycle-accurate engine, from reset
  hybrid    QEMU fast-forwards, then vsim measures the ROI

profile find hot loops under QEMU, configured like the engine (reports --pc-start/--pc-end windows for hybrid)

list    list what is available
  models    the modes and their engines
  engines   discovered cycle-accurate engines

doctor  check toolchain + fixtures are present

global options (every command):
  -h, --help                  this help; after a command, that command's own options and examples
  --version                   the identity of every bundled component (andesim, the shared ABI, qemu, the engine)
  --log-level <0-6>           verbosity, vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off (default 2: program output + the cycle figure)
  --log-file <file>           append EVERY level's messages (timestamped) to <file>; the console keeps --log-level

'andesim <command> --help' lists that command's own options, with examples.

usage: andesim [run] [options] <ELF> [-- <engine args>]

run one simulation (the default: 'run' may be omitted)

modes:
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed
  cycle     one cycle-accurate engine, from reset
  hybrid    QEMU fast-forwards, then vsim measures the ROI

options:
  --mode fast|cycle|hybrid    REQUIRED  which mode to run
  --trigger marker|pc         REQUIRED for hybrid  the ROI delimiter
    --pc-start <sym|0x>       REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI start boundary
    --pc-end <sym|0x>         REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI end boundary
  --engine <id>               pick an engine, e.g. vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default: the sole one)
  --mem-size <spec>           guest RAM, e.g. 256M / 2G (hybrid: max 2G; fast: QEMU -m; cycle: ignored)
  --runtime linux             run a Linux-ABI program (static glibc) under the vlinux proxy kernel; the default is a bare-metal ELF. See runtime/linux/README.md
  --dry-run                   print the exact engine command(s) and exit, running nothing (fast/cycle/hybrid)
  --print-memmap              print the hybrid guest memory map and exit, running nothing (hybrid only; ELF optional)
  --verify                    cross-check the hybrid run against a QEMU oracle
  --kanata <file>             write a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI (hybrid only; open in Konata)
    --objdump <file>          embed that objdump -d dump's disassembly in the trace (requires --kanata)
  --gdb                       pause at startup for a debugger (fast: QEMU stub; cycle: vsim JTAG + $ICEMAN; not hybrid)
  --gdb-port <port>           override the --gdb port (fast 1234, cycle 9104)
  --step-timeout-ms <ms>      hybrid per-leg spawn timeout (default 90000); raise it for a large ROI on the cycle-accurate leg
  -- <args...>                forward everything after -- verbatim to the engine (fast/cycle); hybrid rejects -- args, EXCEPT --runtime linux, where they are app argv

global options (every command):
  -h, --help                  this help; after a command, that command's own options and examples
  --version                   the identity of every bundled component (andesim, the shared ABI, qemu, the engine)
  --log-level <0-6>           verbosity, vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off (default 2: program output + the cycle figure)
  --log-file <file>           append EVERY level's messages (timestamped) to <file>; the console keeps --log-level

examples:
  andesim run --mode fast prog.elf
  andesim --mode fast prog.elf                       # 'run' may be omitted

  andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker prog.elf

  andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2G app.elf -- --threads 1

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Issue #22 -- `--help` is layered, and it is COMPLETE.
3	#
4	#   * `andesim --help` is an OVERVIEW: what the tool is and which commands it
5	#     has. It does not reprint every option of every command.
6	#   * `andesim <cmd> --help` carries that command's COMPLETE option list, plus
7	#     runnable examples.
8	#   * Every option a command ACCEPTS appears in that command's help. An option
9	#     the tool takes but never names cannot be found by a user.
10	#
11	# The accepted set is not a list this file keeps in step by hand. It is
12	# harvested from the option table's own source, and then each candidate is
13	# offered to each command and the BINARY says whether it took it: the parser
14	# finishes before `--help` is honoured, so the probe starts no engine and
15	# needs no ELF.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
19	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
21	
22	require_driver
23	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
24	
25	COMMANDS="run profile list doctor"
26	
27	# --- the candidate options --------------------------------------------------
28	# Every `"--flag"` literal in the parser's own sources. Harvested rather than
29	# listed, so an option added to the parser and forgotten in the help is caught
30	# by this test instead of by a user. `-h` is added by hand: it is the one
31	# single-dash spelling, and no `--` regex can find it.
32	SRCS=()
33	for f in "$ROOT/driver/options.cpp" "$ROOT/driver/cli.cpp"; do
34	  [ -f "$f" ] && SRCS+=("$f")
35	done
36	[ "${#SRCS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no parser source to harvest options from"
37	
38	FLAGS=$( { grep -ohE '"--[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*"' "${SRCS[@]}" | tr -d '"'
39	           echo "-h"; } | sort -u )
40	[ -n "$FLAGS" ] || fail "harvested no options from ${SRCS[*]}"
41	echo "[info] candidate options: $(echo $FLAGS | tr '\n' ' ')"
42	
43	# --- the two questions asked of each (command, option) pair -----------------
44	
45	# accepts CMD FLAG -- true when the PARSER takes FLAG for CMD. A dummy value
46	# follows so a value-taking option is satisfied; a switch simply gains a
47	# positional that `--help` then makes irrelevant. /dev/null is the dummy
48	# because --log-file opens whatever it is handed.
49	accepts() {
50	  local cmd="$1" flag="$2" out
51	  out=$("$BIN" "$cmd" "$flag" /dev/null --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
52	  ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- "unknown option: $flag\$|$flag is not a"
53	}
54	
55	# documented CMD FLAG -- true when CMD's help names FLAG as a whole word, so
56	# `--gdb` is not satisfied by `--gdb-port` and `--llm` is not by `--no-llm`.
57	documented() {
58	  local cmd="$1" flag="$2"
59	  "$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null \
60	    | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)"
61	}
62	
63	# --- 1. every accepted option is discoverable -------------------------------
64	missing=""
65	for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
66	  for flag in $FLAGS; do
67	    accepts "$cmd" "$flag" || continue
68	    documented "$cmd" "$flag" || missing="$missing"$'\n'"  $cmd accepts $flag, '$cmd --help' does not name it"
69	  done
70	done
71	[ -z "$missing" ] || fail "options accepted but undocumented:$missing"
72	ok "every option a command accepts appears in that command's help"
73	
74	# --- 2. each command's help carries runnable examples -----------------------
75	for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
76	  H=$("$BIN" "$cmd" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
77	  printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*andesim ' \
78	    || fail "'$cmd --help' has no runnable example (a line starting 'andesim ...'):"$'\n'"$H"
79	done
80	ok "every command's help carries at least one runnable example"
81	
82	# --- 3. the top level is an overview, not every option ----------------------
83	TOP=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1 </dev/null)
84	for cmd in $COMMANDS; do
85	  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE "^$cmd " \
86	    || fail "the overview does not list the command '$cmd':"$'\n'"$TOP"
87	done
88	# A command's own knobs belong in that command's help. Their presence here is
89	# what "lists every option of every subcommand" looks like.
90	for flag in --pc-start --kanata --gdb-port --min-iters --addr2line --raw; do
91	  printf '%s\n' "$TOP" | grep -qE -- "(^|[^a-z0-9-])$flag([^a-z0-9-]|\$)" \
92	    && fail "the overview reprints a command's own option '$flag':"$'\n'"$TOP"
93	done

95	  || fail "the overview does not point at the per-command help:"$'\n'"$TOP"
96	ok "the top level is an overview: the commands, not every command's options"
97

29	# reports $1 as its own version, the way the real sim_* binaries do.
30	make_fake_engine() {  # <path> <id> <version>
31	  cat >"$1" <<EOF
32	#!/bin/sh
33	[ "\$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}' && exit 0
34	[ "\$1" = "--version" ] && printf 'Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation.\nVersion : $3\n' && exit 0
35	exit 1
36	EOF
37	  chmod +x "$1"
38	}
39	
40	# 1. The command exists, exits 0, and carries one labelled line per component.
41	V=$("$BIN" --version 2>&1); rc=$?
42	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--version rc=$rc want 0:"$'\n'"$V"
43	has '^AndeSim ' "$V"  || fail "--version: no AndeSim line:"$'\n'"$V"
44	has '^  abi '   "$V"  || fail "--version: no abi line:"$'\n'"$V"
45	has '^  qemu '  "$V"  || fail "--version: no qemu line:"$'\n'"$V"
46	has '^  engine ' "$V" || fail "--version: no engine line:"$'\n'"$V"
47	ok "--version: exits 0 with an AndeSim / abi / qemu / engine line"
48	
49	# 2. Build-time half: the AndeSim line carries a SemVer release AND the branch
50	# + short commit of THIS checkout; the abi line carries the branch + short
51	# commit of the shared ABI submodule. Both recorded here independently of the
52	# driver, straight from git.
53	git_id() {  # <dir> -> "<branch>/<short commit>"
54	  local d="$1" b c
55	  c=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null) || return 1
56	  b=$(git -C "$d" symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD 2>/dev/null) ||
57	    b=$(git -C "$d" describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2>/dev/null) ||
58	    b=detached
59	  printf '%s/%s\n' "$b" "$c"
60	}
61	
62	if AS_ID=$(git_id "$ROOT") && ABI_ID=$(git_id "$ROOT/include"); then
63	  has "^AndeSim +v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ \($AS_ID\)$" "$V" ||
64	    fail "--version: AndeSim line should read 'vX.Y.Z ($AS_ID)':"$'\n'"$V"
65	  has "^  abi +$ABI_ID$" "$V" ||
66	    fail "--version: abi line should read '$ABI_ID':"$'\n'"$V"
67	  ok "--version: AndeSim = release + $AS_ID, abi = $ABI_ID (cross-checked against git)"
68	else

70	fi

73	# says about itself, asked here directly.
74	QEMU=$(qemu_bin)
75	if [ -x "$QEMU" ]; then
76	  QV=$("$QEMU" --version 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*version \([0-9][^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)
77	  [ -n "$QV" ] || fail "could not read a version from $QEMU"
78	  has "^  qemu +$QV$" "$V" || fail "--version: qemu line should read '$QV':"$'\n'"$V"
79	  ok "--version: qemu = $QV (cross-checked against $QEMU itself)"
80	else
81	  echo "[skip] qemu cross-check: no $QEMU"
82	fi

85	# use says about itself. Pinned to ONE real engine via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR so
86	# the expected line is unambiguous.

88	if [ -x "$SIM" ]; then

90	  [ -n "$EV" ] || fail "could not read a version from $SIM"
91	  mkdir -p "$TMP/one"; ln -sf "$SIM" "$TMP/one/sim_pinned"
92	  E=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/one" "$BIN" --version 2>&1); rc=$?
93	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--version rc=$rc want 0:"$'\n'"$E"
94	  [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$E" | grep -c '^  engine ')" -eq 1 ] ||

97	    fail "--version: engine line should read '$EV':"$'\n'"$E"
98	  ok "--version: engine = $EV (cross-checked against $SIM itself)"
99	
100	  # ... and with the real engines dir, where every sim_* comes out of one vsim
101	  # build and so reports the same commit, that value is stated ONCE. Eight
102	  # identical lines would be noise.
103	  [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -c '^  engine ')" -eq 1 ] ||
104	    fail "--version: engines agreeing on a version must collapse to one line:"$'\n'"$V"
105	  has "^  engine +$EV$" "$V" ||
106	    fail "--version: the single engine line should read '$EV':"$'\n'"$V"
107	  ok "--version: all real engines agree -> the commit is reported once, unadorned"
108	else

110	fi

113	# in a binary that reports a different version changes the line, nothing else.

115	make_fake_engine "$TMP/a/sim_fake" "verilator:fakecfg" "87a0baa"

git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(cli): one option table drives both parsing and help (behavioral)

There were two lists -- the parser's, of what andesim accepts, and help's,
of what it advertises -- and nothing held them together. --runtime and the
whole profile report set were accepted and never mentioned, and every
command silently accepted every other command's options: `andesim run
--limit 5` parsed cleanly and did nothing.

driver/options.cpp now describes each option once: its spelling, arity,
destination, the commands that take it, and the text help prints. The
parser reads one half of a row and help the other, so an option that
exists is an option that prints.

The help becomes two layers, as issue #22 asks. `andesim --help` is an
overview -- the commands and what each is for. `andesim <cmd> --help`
carries that command's complete option list, the globals, and runnable
examples. cmd_profile's hand-written copy of the run-only list is gone;
the parser rejects a foreign option and names the command that takes it.

tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_help_complete.sh harvests the accepted set
from the table's own source, asks the binary which options each command
takes, and fails on any the help does not name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 kernel A/Bs:
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# AndeSim

AndeSim gives a cycle count for code that you write yourself.

Put two markers in your C function, around the part that you want to
measure. AndeSim runs the program in QEMU at full speed, then measures
the marked region on a cycle-accurate model of an Andes RISC-V core.
The result is one number: the cycles between the two markers.

AndeSim supports 64-bit RISC-V only.

## Prerequisites

Get these four things before you start.

**A container runtime.** A run always happens inside the AndeSim image.
Use podman to build the image; `docker build` cannot mount the toolchain.
Use podman or docker to run the image. On macOS, also start the machine
with `podman machine init && podman machine start`.

**Read access to the Andes RD-SW repositories on gitea.andestech.com.**
The image build gets the RTL of the cycle-accurate core from these
repositories. Put your credentials in `~/.git-credentials`. The build
stops immediately if it cannot read a repository.

**An Andes RISC-V bare-metal toolchain (rv64).** The toolchain directory
must contain `bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc`. AndeSim does not include a
toolchain. Your toolchain compiles your program, and the image build
uses it too. The build mounts the toolchain read-only, and never copies
it into the image.

**Disk space and time.** The image is about 1.8 GB. The build compiles
QEMU and Verilates the RTL of the core, so it takes hours. You do this
one time.

## 1. Build the image

```sh
git clone https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git andesim
cd andesim
scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain /path/to/riscv-toolchain
```

Write your own toolchain directory in place of
`/path/to/riscv-toolchain`. The build makes an image with the name
`andesim:v0.1.0`.

All the other steps below start in this `andesim` directory.

## 2. Build the runtime library

```sh
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/riscv-toolchain
scripts/build_runtime.sh
```

This step takes seconds. It makes `build/runtime/`, which holds the C
runtime that your program links against, and the marker header
`andesim/ROI.h`.

## 3. Write a function to measure

Put this in `kernel.c`:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define N 256
static int a[N], b[N];

/* noinline keeps the loop inside the measured region: the markers hold
   memory accesses in place, but not work that stays in registers. */
__attribute__((noinline)) static long dot(const int *x, const int *y, int n)
{
        long s = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
                s += (long)x[i] * y[i];
        return s;
}

int main(void)
{
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = N - i; }

        andesim_ROI_begin();
        long s = dot(a, b, N);
        andesim_ROI_end();

        printf("dot = %ld\n", s);
        return 0;
}
```

The two markers are RISC-V HINT instructions. Every core reads them as a
NOP, so the same binary also runs on other simulators and on silicon.

## 4. Compile it

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc \
    -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
    -I build/runtime/include -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs \
    kernel.c -o kernel.elf
```

The two flags `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` link the AndeSim
runtime. They give you `printf`, `exit` and the other standard C
functions.

## 5. Measure it

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker kernel.elf
```

The answer is the last line:

```
[andesim] 1622 cycles
```

`./andesim` starts the container for you. It mounts the current
directory at the same path inside the image, so a relative path such as
`kernel.elf` works as usual.

Hybrid mode stops at the end marker, so the program does not reach its
`printf`. To see the output of the program, run it in fast mode:

```sh
./andesim run --mode fast kernel.elf
```

## Run modes

| Mode | What it does | What you get |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| `fast` | QEMU runs the whole program. | The output of the program, at full speed. |
| `cycle` | The cycle-accurate engine runs the whole program from reset. | The output of the program, and the cycles of the whole run. |
| `hybrid` | QEMU runs up to the start marker, then the cycle-accurate engine measures the region. | The cycles of the marked region only. |

Use `--trigger pc --pc-start <symbol> --pc-end <symbol>` to mark a region
by address instead of by marker, when you cannot edit the source.

`andesim profile prog.elf` finds the hot loops of a program and reports
the regions that are worth a hybrid measurement.

## Linux programs

To run a Linux program (a static glibc binary such as `llama-completion`)
instead of a bare-metal ELF, read
[runtime/linux/README.md](runtime/linux/README.md).

## Help

```sh
andesim --help              # the commands
andesim run --help          # every option of run, with examples
```

Every option that AndeSim accepts appears in the help of the command
that accepts it.

| `cycle` | The cycle-accurate engine runs the whole program from reset. | The output of the program, and the cycles of the whole run. |
| `hybrid` | QEMU runs up to the start marker, then the cycle-accurate engine measures the region. | The cycles of the marked region only. |

Use `--trigger pc --pc-start <symbol> --pc-end <symbol>` to mark a region
by address instead of by marker, when you cannot edit the source.

`andesim profile prog.elf` finds the hot loops of a program and reports
the regions that are worth a hybrid measurement.

## Linux programs

To run a Linux program (a static glibc binary such as `llama-completion`)
instead of a bare-metal ELF, read
[runtime/linux/README.md](runtime/linux/README.md).

```sh
andesim --help              # the commands
andesim run --help          # every option of run, with examples
```

Every option that AndeSim accepts appears in the help of the command
that accepts it.

input.content:
# Changelog

This changelog starts at v0.1.0, the first AndeSim release. The history
before v0.1.0 is not reconstructed here.

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).

## v0.1.0

The first release. AndeSim gives a cycle count for a marked region of
your own code, on a cycle-accurate model of an Andes RISC-V core.

### Added

- **Three run modes.** `fast` runs the whole program in QEMU. `cycle`
  runs the whole program on the cycle-accurate engine, from reset.
  `hybrid` lets QEMU run up to the start of the region, then measures
  the region on the cycle-accurate engine.
- **Two region triggers.** `--trigger marker` reads the
  `andesim_ROI_begin()` and `andesim_ROI_end()` HINT instructions from
  `andesim/ROI.h`. `--trigger pc` takes a symbol or an address, for a
  program that you cannot change.
- **One image holds everything.** `scripts/build_image.sh` builds an
  image that carries QEMU, the cycle-accurate engine, the handoff
  plugin, the driver and the runtime library. Each source is pinned by
  commit. The build context is empty, so no file from the build machine
  enters the image. Users prepare nothing themselves.
- **A run always happens in that image**, on Linux and on macOS. Both
  legs of a hybrid run must share one Linux kernel. `./andesim` starts
  the container, mounts the current directory at the same path, and
  sizes `/dev/shm` from the `--mem-size` of the run.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the AE350 RAM windows -- DRAM (2G) + DRAM_EXT (14G) = 16 GiB --
#           MINUS that page (U10f). 16G therefore overflows and is rejected.
#           2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that still fits the LOW window,
#           keeping the historical flat-from-zero map; anything above it moves
#           DRAM to the high view at 0x8_00000000 with a low 2G alias, so old
#           and new cycle figures stay comparable. See driver/shm.cpp
#           max_program_mem_bytes() / hybrid_ram_base().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size, the retired spelling, is gone: an option no help mentions
#           cannot be discovered (issue #22).
set -uo pipefail
=== driver cap ===
90:long long max_program_mem_bytes() {
91-  // U10f: the contiguous high view -- DRAM alias (2G) + DRAM_EXT (14G) from
92-  // 0x8_00000000 -- with the scratch page on top. At or below the low window
93-  // the flat-from-zero map is kept (hybrid_ram_base decides which).
94-  constexpr long long kAe350RamWindowsBytes = 16LL * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
95-  return kAe350RamWindowsBytes - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
96-}
97-
98-uint64_t hybrid_ram_base(long long mem_bytes) {
99-  // Keep the historical flat-from-zero map while program + scratch fit the
100-  // low window: every cycle number recorded there stays comparable.
101-  const long long low_window = 2LL * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
102-  return physical_mmap_bytes(mem_bytes) <= low_window ? 0u : 0x800000000ull;
103-}
104-
105-std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Issue #24 contract, verified against a built image: what the image actually
# contains. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_build.sh covers the build
# plan; this covers the product of that plan.
#
# Skips when the image has not been built on this machine -- building it takes
# hours (Verilating the RTL), so it cannot be a precondition of the standard
# suite. Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, then this runs for real.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")}"

RUNTIME="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$RUNTIME" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=docker
  else ok "no container runtime here -- skipping image contents"; exit 0
  fi
fi

if ! "$RUNTIME" image exists "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "$IMAGE not built here -- skipping image contents (scripts/build_image.sh)"
  exit 0
fi

# in_image CMD...  -- run a shell command inside the image, nothing mounted.
in_image() {
  "$RUNTIME" run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "$IMAGE" -c "$1" 2>&1
}

# --- the image runs AndeSim with no QEMU and no engine prepared outside ------
out=$(in_image '/opt/andesim/andesim list engines')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qw "$ENGINE" \
  || fail "the image does not report the $ENGINE engine:"$'\n'"$out"

# Exactly one cycle-accurate engine. Every other config is deferred, and each
# one would add a Verilator run to the slowest step of the build.
engines=$(in_image 'ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR" | grep "^sim_" | sort')
[ "$engines" = "sim_$ENGINE" ] \
  || fail "the image must hold sim_$ENGINE and nothing else, found:"$'\n'"$engines"

out=$(in_image '"$VSIM_QEMU" --version')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'qemu' \
  || fail "the image's QEMU does not run:"$'\n'"$out"

# The handoff plugin and the runtime library are AndeSim's own artifacts; the
# runtime library existing proves the mounted toolchain built it.
in_image 'test -f "$VSIM_PLUGIN"' \
  || fail "the hybrid handoff plugin is missing from the image"
in_image 'test -f /opt/andesim/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a' \
  || fail "the runtime library is missing -- the build-time toolchain mount failed"

# --- the toolchain is the user's, mounted; the image carries neither it nor -
# --- any path from the machine that built the image -------------------------
# The mount point exists and is empty. Existing matters: a missing directory
# gave "No such file or directory" with nothing in the image to hint at what
# to mount, where an empty one shows the shape the run expects.
in_image "test -d $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN" \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN does not exist, so a forgotten mount says only" \
          " 'No such file or directory'"
left=$(in_image "ls -A $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN | wc -l")
[ "$left" = "0" ] \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN holds $left entries -- a toolchain was baked in"

# The entry point the image declares must be there and runnable.
in_image 'test -x /opt/andesim/andesim' \
  || fail "the image's ENTRYPOINT /opt/andesim/andesim is missing or not executable"

cfg=$(in_image 'cat /opt/andesim/config.env')
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq "^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN\$" \
  || fail "the image's config.env does not name the mount point:"$'\n'"$cfg"
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq '/local/|/home/' \
  && fail "the image's config.env carries a host path:"$'\n'"$cfg"

in_image 'test -e /opt/andesim/.git' \
  && fail "the image carries the repository's git history"

ok "image contents: driver + QEMU + exactly the $ENGINE engine, no baked toolchain"
